title: Republic of Brazil
capsule: The Republic of Brazil denotes the democratic federal state founded on the 1988 Constitution—drafted by an elected Constituent Assembly and promulgated 5 October 1988—which restored direct presidential elections (first held in 1989), guaranteed civil liberties, and has governed Brazil through the Cardoso, Lula, Rousseff, Temer, Bolsonaro and second Lula administrations into the 2020s. It survived the 1992 impeachment of Fernando Collor and the 2016 impeachment of Dilma Rousseff without constitutional rupture, marking Latin America's longest continuous democratic period. This post-1988 constitutional order is distinct from the earlier oligarchic, centralized and military-authoritarian phases sharing this Wikidata identifier.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Brazil's national territory is precisely bounded by settled international agreements; the polity entry reflects a political-regime periodization of a continuous state, so territorial confidence is high, though the dataset geometry is essentially that of modern Brazil throughout this span. Capsule researched for this polity/era specifically (confidence: high).
